questions.question: 9. The total population of Kenya in 2009 was 38.6 million and its total land area is 576,076 km² if 26.1 milling of the total population is rural and 45200 km². If the total land area is cultivated. What would be the agricultural density?
questions.answer_guide: Agricultural density = rural population ÷ cultivated land = 26,100,000 ÷ 45,200 ≈ 577 persons/km²

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
1.
  a. Evaluate why the growing conditions of sugar cane is appropriate favorable in tropical, sub-tropical or temperate regions (2 Marks)
  b. state any two characteristics of postural farming (2 Marks)
  c. identify any two problems facing pastoralism in Somaliland (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Sugar cane grows best in tropical and sub-tropical regions because it needs high temperatures (about 21–27 °C), heavy rainfall or irrigation (1,500 mm+), a long growing season of 12–18 months without frost, and a dry sunny period before harvest to raise sugar content. Temperate regions are unsuitable because of frost and short summers.
b. (read as pastoral farming) Any two: keeping livestock (camels, cattle, sheep, goats) as the main activity; movement in search of pasture and water (nomadism); large herds kept for prestige and subsistence; found in dry/semi-arid areas.
c. Any two: recurrent drought and water shortage; overgrazing and land degradation; livestock diseases; poor marketing and low prices/export bans; conflicts over pasture and water; land enclosure.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
2.
  a. Describe any two disadvantages of solar energy (2 Marks)
  b. Explain any two advantages of wind energy (2 Marks)
  c. List any two non-renewable energy services (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any two: high initial cost of panels and batteries; not available at night and reduced on cloudy days; needs large areas for big power stations; storage is expensive.
b. Any two: renewable/inexhaustible; clean – no pollution or greenhouse gases; cheap to run once installed; suitable for remote windy areas (e.g. Somaliland coast).
c. Any two: coal, petroleum (oil), natural gas, uranium (nuclear fuel).

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
3.
  a. Mention any two modes of transport among the common modes of transport. (2 Marks)
  b. Describe any two roles of transport and communication in the economic development of Africa. (2 Marks)
  c. Identify any two types of trade (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any two: land transport (road, rail), water transport (sea, river), air transport, pipeline transport.
b. Any two: moves raw materials to industries and goods to markets; promotes trade (local and international); creates employment; opens up remote areas and links countries (regional integration); helps spread of information, education and tourism.
c. Any two: internal (home) trade and international (external) trade; or bilateral and multilateral trade; or visible and invisible trade; wholesale and retail trade.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
4.
  a. List and describe the three branches of Somaliland government (3 Marks)
  b. State any two types of government (2 Marks)
  c. Which branch of government has the responsibility/authority to remove the president from the position/office (1 Mark)
questions.answer_guide:
a. The Legislature (Parliament: House of Representatives and House of Elders/Guurti) – makes laws and approves the budget.
   The Executive (President, Vice-President and Council of Ministers) – implements laws and runs the government.
   The Judiciary (courts headed by the Supreme Court) – interprets laws and settles disputes.
b. Any two: democracy, monarchy, dictatorship, republic, theocracy, oligarchy.
c. The Legislature (Parliament), through impeachment.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
5.
  a. If the number of birth in a community in 1980 was 18,247 and the mid-year population of was 985,210, what is the crude birth rate of this community? (2 Marks)
  b. Assume the total number of live births in a given year is 65 and the total number of women in the childbearing age (15 - 49) is 2032 find the general fertility rate. (2 Marks)
  c. The number of death in a county in 2009 was 14,129 and the mid-year population was 864,420. What was the crude death rate of that country (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. CBR = births ÷ mid-year population × 1000 = 18,247 ÷ 985,210 × 1000 ≈ 18.5 per 1000
b. GFR = live births ÷ women aged 15–49 × 1000 = 65 ÷ 2032 × 1000 ≈ 32 per 1000 women
c. CDR = deaths ÷ mid-year population × 1000 = 14,129 ÷ 864,420 × 1000 ≈ 16.3 per 1000

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
6.
  a. List any four factors affecting the exploration of minerals (2 Marks)
  b. Describe any two methods of mining (2 Marks)
  c. Explain any two effects of mining on the environment (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Any four: size of the deposit; quality (grade) of the ore; depth/mode of occurrence; availability of capital and technology; transport and accessibility; market demand and prices; government policy and political stability; availability of labour.
b. Any two: open-cast (open-pit) mining – removing overburden to dig minerals near the surface; underground (shaft/drift) mining – digging shafts and tunnels to reach deep deposits; alluvial/placer mining – washing minerals from river sands and gravels; quarrying.
c. Any two: destruction of vegetation and landscape (derelict land, open pits); soil erosion; pollution of air, water and soil by dust and chemicals; noise; loss of wildlife habitats; land subsidence.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
7.
  a. Explain the following terms?
     i. Mean daily temperature (1 Mark)
     ii. Annual temperature range (1 Mark)
  b. State any two heat transfer process of energy (2 Marks)
  c. Explain any two characteristics of polar climate (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. i. Mean daily temperature = (maximum + minimum temperature of the day) ÷ 2.
   ii. Annual temperature range = mean temperature of the hottest month − mean temperature of the coldest month.
b. Any two: conduction, convection, radiation (also advection).
c. Any two: very cold all year (warmest month below 10 °C); long dark winters and short cool summers; very low precipitation, mostly snow; ground permanently frozen (permafrost) or covered by ice; strong winds and blizzards; little or no vegetation (tundra).

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
8.
  a. What is the aerial photography? (2 Marks)
  b. Explain any two applications of aerial photography. (2 Marks)
  c. What are the contour lines? (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Aerial photography is the taking of photographs of the earth's surface from an elevated position, such as an aircraft, drone or balloon.
b. Any two: map making and updating maps; land-use and town planning; surveying for roads, dams and mineral exploration; monitoring environmental change (deforestation, floods, erosion); military reconnaissance; agricultural and forest surveys.
c. Contour lines are imaginary lines drawn on a map joining places of the same height (elevation) above sea level.

questions.answer_guide:
a. It is a food web – several interconnected food chains showing how energy flows from the sun to the plant and then through herbivores to carnivores.
b. The sun is the source of energy; plants use sunlight to make food by photosynthesis.
c. Producer: the plant. Consumers: rabbit, grasshopper and mouse (primary/secondary), snake and hawk/eagle (higher consumers). Decomposers: the ants/micro-organisms (bacteria, fungi) breaking down dead matter.
d. The snake population would decrease because one of its food sources is lost; snakes would compete more for mice and grasshoppers, which would then also decline.

questions.section: PART TWO: Structured Questions (60 Marks) – Answer all the following questions. Each question carries 6 marks
questions.question:
10.
  a. Explain the main types of igneous rocks. (2 Marks)
  b. Describe any two plate bounders or plate margins. (2 Marks)
  c. Explain the two main types of the forces which produce the physical features of the earth's surface? (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
a. Intrusive (plutonic) igneous rocks – magma cools slowly inside the earth, forming large crystals (e.g. granite). Extrusive (volcanic) igneous rocks – lava cools quickly on the surface, forming small crystals (e.g. basalt).
b. Any two: constructive (divergent) margins – plates move apart and new crust forms (e.g. Mid-Atlantic Ridge, East African Rift); destructive (convergent) margins – plates collide and one is subducted, forming fold mountains, trenches and volcanoes; conservative (transform) margins – plates slide past each other (e.g. San Andreas Fault).
c. Internal (endogenic) forces – from inside the earth: folding, faulting, earthquakes and volcanism, which build up landforms. External (exogenic) forces – on the surface: weathering, erosion and deposition by water, wind and ice, which wear down landforms.
